12.0.s.en: (1) Judith's prayers and fasts in the camp of Holofernes

12.0.0.en: After the first meeting between Judith and Holofernes, in which she won his great admiration for her beauty and his esteem for her wisdom, so that he agreed with her in all that she said and even declared his readiness to follow her God, because of the holiness he saw in her and her devotion to this God who would give him victory, Holofernes ordered that a dwelling be prepared for her in the best of places, far from the tents of the soldiers and officers, beside the storehouses of his treasures of gold, silver and precious stones. To honor her he also ordered that she be served the finest food and drink, from what was served to him personally.

12.1.0.en: But Judith, with all strength and trust in her God, refused to partake of his food and drink, because partaking of them was counted a sin according to the law of her God. Rather she resolved to eat what she had brought with her, of food prepared according to her law.

12.1.1.en: May you have faith and hold fast to the commandment, however embarrassing the surrounding circumstances. Do not be afraid to declare that worldly food, or speech, or dress does not suit you, but is counted as sin and a stumbling block before God, even though others do it. God must be obeyed rather than men, and be sure that God will give you favor in their eyes, so that they will not prevent you from carrying out the commandment.

12.2.0.en: As your soul lives: a phrase said not only as a prayer for life but as an oath, that is, "By your life, what I say must be accomplished." Of course the Law permitted oaths in the Old Testament.

12.2.1.en: Out of concern for Judith and love for her, Holofernes asked what she would do, and from where she would get food when what she had with her ran out. Judith replied with full confidence that it would not run out until God accomplished her mission and what she was thinking of. Before this confidence and strength and the grace of God working in her, Holofernes agreed with her and was silent, and then they brought her into her tent. Holofernes thought that what she was thinking of was the surrender of the city to him, but she was thinking of God, who would save her people by her hands. Perhaps Holofernes' trust in Judith's holiness, and that she was a prophetess of the gods, made him submit to her words, which came out of her mouth quietly but with great power.

12.2.2.en: Do you have such trust in God, who protects you, surrounds you and saves you from any affliction, whatever the material obstacles? The strength of your faith silences the wicked, so that they do not resist you.

12.3.0.en: After Judith had surveyed the place of the tent and what was in it, she felt that it was suitable for her to stay in and to fulfil her worship in quiet, but that it was far from the springs of water that she needed for washing before completing her prayers, according to the Mosaic Law. So she asked Holofernes for permission to go down to the valley below the mountain on which her city stood, to wash there, since her tent, the tent of Holofernes, and the tents of his treasuries were on a hill above that valley. She asked this permission for three days only, as is understood from (v. 6), since she believed that God would intervene after that and save His people out of compassion for them, before the five days that they had set earlier, according to the divine revelation to which we referred (ch. 11:13). The period of three days points to the number of the Holy Trinity, that is, the perfection of the divine work, which is stronger and swifter than human striving, to which the number five points, in reference to human striving and the five Mosaic sacrifices. For the work of God is stronger and swifter than what the human heart imagines.

12.3.1.en: Judith's piety appears in her holding fast to prayer not only during the day but in the last watch, that is, the last part of the night, and then she continued praying throughout the day. She prayed night and day with fasting, asceticism and purification with water according to the Law. We note her exactness in washing: she did not wash with the water found among the Assyrians, but with the water of the springs belonging to her city. To this degree she was exact.

12.4.0.en: From the depth of Holofernes' admiration for Judith and his conviction of her connection with her God, he agreed without the slightest doubt about her, although the springs of water in which she would wash were close to her city, as appears from (v. 7).

12.4.1.en: Do not be ashamed to hold fast to the commandments of God, and to all that the fulfilment of those commandments requires. God will give you favor in the eyes of others and will prepare suitable circumstances for you to live with Him, even if the purposes of others differ and their thoughts are evil, far from God.

12.5.0.en: On the next day Judith began, in the early morning, to wash at the spring of water in the valley of Bethulia, then she would go up to her tent and continue prayer and fasting until evening, in tears, humility and supplication to God, as though she were in her upper room in her house continuing her devotional life and eating her ascetic food. Then she would pray and rest during the night, to wake on the following day... and so she continued her worship as though she were living in a monastery and not in the midst of the camp of the enemies.

12.5.1.en: How strong is your faith and your prayers, Judith, and your holding to fasting with all rigor! You put us to shame, we who are negligent, making excuses to God because of the circumstances, problems and pressures of life.

12.6.s.en: (2) Holofernes invites Judith to spend the night with him

12.6.0.en: After the end of the three days that Judith spent in fasting, prayers and fervent worship, waiting for God to declare His will, the surprise came: Holofernes made a supper, that is, a banquet for his servants. Of course the servants meant here are his close officers, and not all his army, whose number was one hundred and fifty thousand soldiers. He held this banquet to express his joy at the near victory, and hoping to spend his night with Judith, whose captivating beauty had taken possession of his heart.

12.6.1.en: The difference appears clearly between the thinking of the children of God and the children of the world as they prepare for great deeds: the children of God take refuge in Him with fervent prayers and strong fasts, while the wicked are absorbed in their pleasures. Thus afflictions lead us to spiritual growth, while they lead the wicked to various sins. Holofernes sent his eunuch called "Bagoas" (he was the head of his private guard; the guard was chosen from eunuchs possessing bodily strength, so that Holofernes could enjoy himself and plunge into his lusts without fear of him concerning his women). This confirms the absorption of the wicked and their careful planning to satisfy their bodily pleasures and indulge in delights. He sent him in the evening to Judith, that she might agree to spend the night in his tent, with him on his bed, without using force or compulsion, since it is a disgrace and shame among the Assyrians for a woman to leave them without their lying with her.

12.7.0.en: So Bagoas went to her, in awe of her holiness and goodness, and told her of Holofernes' desire, asking her to agree without shame or refusal, since this is the usual and natural thing among the Assyrians. He encouraged her that her lying with Holofernes would give her great honor, to be one of his maidservants, so that she would eat and drink with him, that is, be among those nearest to him. Thus we see the extent of Holofernes' lust, matched by the chastity and holiness of Judith, and this is the reason for Holofernes' defeat, for he was defeated by his lust and by the chastity of Judith.

12.7.1.en: How strange are the thoughts of men! They not only fall into sins, but regard that as something ordinary and boast of it, and purity and uprightness have become shame and disgrace. To such a degree does the devil control their lives and thoughts. So beware lest your thoughts mix with theirs, lest you be polluted or lose some of your principles, and then justify your sins and thus close upon yourself the door of repentance, since you have become permissive.

12.8.0.en: Good: he sees it as good.

12.8.1.en: It was an extremely difficult situation for Judith. Would she hold fast to her purity and refuse to submit to the pressing desires and lusts of Holofernes, which were for him something logical and natural? Or would she agree and give up her purity? ... Nothing helped her in this critical situation except her prayers and worship over the three days, and indeed what had preceded that in her house.

12.8.2.en: We believe that God's earlier revelation to her of the details of her secret mission, and that Holofernes would ask her to spend the night with him, kept her from being astonished at Bagoas' request, so she agreed with all welcome and humility, expressing that it was a great honor for her, in which she would take pride all her life. This is a high degree of faith that surpasses reason, so that she became a symbol of the Virgin Mary, who agreed to be betrothed to the one the priests would choose, to live in his house, while she longed to be a virgin, and because of her faith that bewilders minds, God indeed chose for her St. Joseph the carpenter, the aged man, who would care for her while she kept her virginity.

12.8.3.en: It is noticed that at the end of her words about Holofernes she said, "Whatever pleases him, that will be very good to me all the days of my life." She sees in Holofernes' sensual, evil desire the means God uses to complete His plan to deliver His people from the hand of the Assyrians, so she continues to glorify God all the days of her life, who used this evil desire. For God's plan is always good and worthy of glory.

12.9.s.en: (3) Judith in the tent of Holofernes and his drinking of wine

12.9.0.en: After Judith's agreement to Bagoas, she put on beautiful, shining garments and adorned herself with all her adornment, as she had done three days before at the first meeting with Holofernes.

12.9.1.en: She prepared with her maidservant supper food for the two of them, and they went with Bagoas to the great tent of Holofernes. Bagoas went in and told Holofernes of Judith's coming to him, and he rejoiced greatly. Then she was brought in to him in his bedchamber, and her maidservant remained with some guards and officers in the outer reception room. When he saw her he was dazzled by her beauty, and his lusts were stirred violently and strongly, for he had longed to see her this night.

12.9.2.en: These were terrible moments through which Judith passed. She had no helper except God who dwelt in her, who supported her and gave her strength, steadfastness and irresistible beauty to accomplish His will.

12.9.3.en: Be sure, my brother, that when people leave you, you will feel the help of God, whom you seek more than at any other time, and He increases you in strength and gives you favor in the eyes of others, even if they want to do you harm.

12.10.1.en: After Bagoas departed, Judith was standing alone before Holofernes, who was sitting on his bed, and he said to her, "Sit down now and eat and drink, for I admire you, and you have found favor in my eyes." Judith obeyed, with all steadfastness, confidence, gentleness and humility before Holofernes, giving him to eat and drink first, and declaring her deep joy on this great day, the like of which she had not known in all her days. She meant, of course, that with the eye of faith she saw the salvation of God that would be accomplished by her hands, by destroying this man and rescuing her people. But this wicked man, in the excess of his pride, did not doubt her admiration for him, and that she felt proud to accompany him and to spend the night with him.

12.10.2.en: Beware of pride, for it blinds the eyes of a person, so that his thoughts are deceived and he loses his wisdom, and indeed his whole life.

12.11.0.en: Then she went out to the reception room, took pieces of fleece and spread them on the ground (as mentioned in the translation of the Jesuit Fathers), and set out the food and drink that her maidservant had prepared for her (as the Jewish law allows), and sat down to eat and drink. Of course the wine she had brought with her was grape juice, only lightly fermented, not intoxicating, and not causing a person to lose consciousness, although it looked to Holofernes like any wine.

12.11.1.en: Holofernes allowed her to eat her food and drink her drink, as we mentioned before, out of the excess of his admiration for her, because of the grace of God working in her.

12.12.0.en: Before her: near her and facing her.

12.12.1.en: As for him, his joy increased at her being with him, and as he was reassured by her obedience to him and her sitting before him in a gentle manner, eating and drinking, the fires of lust blazed in him violently. He lost his balance and began to drink without awareness, in large quantities, as he had never done in all his life. Judith was very beautiful, and God increased her beauty in his eyes and put into his heart a sense of safety from her, and he lost control over himself and went on drinking without restraint.

12.12.2.en: How did Holofernes rush to drink wine to this degree? What drove him but his evil lusts and the corruption of his impure heart? God permitted this so that his evil would come upon his own head, and that He might deliver His people from his hands.

12.12.3.en: The sin of the sinner comes upon his own head before it touches others. So let us hasten to repentance, to protect ourselves from sin and receive forgiveness in the sacrament of confession, and to protect others from our harming them by our sin.

12.12.4.en: The killing of Holofernes and the escape of Judith (1) The cutting off of Holofernes' head (vv. 1-10)

12.12.5.en: 1- And when evening came, his servants made haste to their homes, and Bagoas closed the doors of the bedchamber and went away. 2- They were all weighed down with wine. 3- And Judith was alone in the bedchamber. 4- And Holofernes was lying on the bed asleep, because of his great drunkenness. 5- And Judith commanded her maidservant to stand outside before the bedchamber and keep watch.

12.12.6.en: 6- And Judith stood before the bed, and she was praying with tears and moving her lips in silence. 7- And she said, Strengthen me, O Lord God of Israel, and look in this hour upon the work of my hands, that Jerusalem Your city may rise up as You promised, and that I may accomplish what I have resolved, trusting that I can do it by Your help. 8- And when she had said this she came near to the pillar that was at the head of his bed, and loosed his dagger that hung there tied to it. 9- And she drew it, and took hold of the hair of his head, and said, Strengthen me, O Lord God, in this hour. 10- Then she struck twice upon his neck and cut off his head, and pulled down the canopy of his bed from the pillars, and rolled his body off the bed.

13.0.s.en: (3) Judith in the tent of Holofernes and his drinking of wine

13.0.0.en: After Bagoas had performed his task and succeeded in easily bringing Judith willingly to the bedchamber of his master, and the minutes passed quietly while he heard from afar the whispers of conversation between his master and Judith, he dismissed the private guard of Holofernes' tent, who had begun to drink in celebration of this night in which their master had granted them the right to revelry and carousing, while he himself enjoyed the company of the beautiful Judith.

13.0.1.en: Perhaps Judith confirmed the permission she had received to wash at the springs of Bethulia at the end of the night, before dawn, so she asked Bagoas' leave, saying that after spending the night with Holofernes she would go as usual to wash at the springs of water beside her city "Bethulia." He allowed her and informed the guards of the camp of this. Then Bagoas felt that there was no need for his presence and that it was better to leave his master in his seclusion with Judith. So he closed the door of the tent upon them, left Judith's maidservant in the reception room, and departed, to enjoy for himself also the delicious food and abundant drink at the banquet.

13.1.0.en: Judith found herself alone in the bedchamber of Holofernes, who, from drinking so much wine, had thrown himself on his bed and sunk into a deep sleep.

13.1.1.en: Wonderful are Your plans, O Lord! You prepared for Your servant Judith everything that would help her to perform her mission. You made Holofernes, out of the intensity of his admiration for her, drink to excess and far exceed the amount he was accustomed to drink, so he lost consciousness completely and slept deeply. As for his soldiers, they were busy with revelry, drunkenness and eating, and forgot their caution and left their guarding of the tent. Even Bagoas, You put reassurance in his heart, so he too went away to the banquet, leaving his master unguarded, confident that he was immersed in his pleasures with the beautiful Judith.

13.1.2.en: Advance in your spiritual practices of prayers, fasts and readings, and also in serving God with enthusiasm, confident that God will help you and arrange everything to fulfil His will in you, because He desires your salvation more than you desire it, and He Himself is the One who works in the service, while you are merely an instrument to share with Him the joy of the salvation of the souls of others.

13.2.1.en: When Judith found the enemy of God fallen in deep sleep, with God having prepared for her all the means and the atmosphere entirely clear for her, she went out and made sure herself that her maidservant was sitting alone in the reception room, that there was not a single guard at the door, and that everyone had disappeared inside the tents, eating, drinking and revelling. She commanded her maidservant to stand beside the outer door of the tent and to listen carefully for any sound or approaching footsteps. Although God had arranged everything, Judith did her duty with exactness and complete caution, not relying idly on Him. Although God alone is able to kill and destroy Holofernes, she must do her duty fully. So too Christ was able to raise Lazarus, yet they had first to remove the stone.

13.2.2.en: Do not be negligent in your spiritual striving, in your prayers, fasts and readings, and leave no gap for sin to enter you. Then God will fulfil His will in you, and Satan your enemy will fall prostrate under your feet.

13.3.0.en: Then Judith entered the bedchamber a second time, with Holofernes lying before her on his bed, and she lifted her eyes toward heaven in a prayer from the depth of the heart. Her voice was not heard in it, but it appeared in the moving of her lips and her tears flowing down her cheeks, as she asked God in the most critical moment of her life. Here appears the extent of her humility, her feeling of weakness and need of God, and her trust in His power that supported her. There was not a single atom of a feeling of reliance on herself, on her own person and her beauty, in this service, but her reliance was wholly on God.

13.4.0.en: Rise up: rescue, raise and lift up His people from their humiliation.

13.4.1.en: She reminded Him that He is the God of Israel and that His city is Jerusalem, and asked Him to fulfil His promises to protect His children. Let Him bless her work now with the salvation of His people, to be rid of Holofernes their enemy, for she believed that His power was able to help her to accomplish her difficult mission with which God had charged her.

13.4.2.en: God rejoices when you ask Him to fulfil His promises, declare your sonship to Him and your holding to Him alone, and press Him to save you from all your sins and troubles.

13.5.0.en: His dagger: it was the custom of kings and chiefs to hang a weapon by their beds to defend themselves, and this dagger was not an ordinary dagger but resembled a small sword, to befit the rank of its owner.

13.5.1.en: Drew it: took it out of its sheath.

13.5.2.en: The canopy of his bed: the mosquito net, a large cloth covering that covers the bed, placed on its four posts, to keep insects off those lying on the bed.

13.5.3.en: After this Judith stepped forward, her strong faith having given her extraordinary courage to accomplish a very difficult mission, contrary to her gentle nature, since she had spent her whole life in quiet inside her house, and after her widowhood she had devoted herself to prayers and meditations.

13.5.4.en: God gives strength to accomplish His work, even if it is strange and contrary to the nature of the person who performs it, as Jeremiah, who had delicate feelings, rebuked his people and all the rulers, shepherds and priests, and likewise David, the ruddy youth with beautiful eyes, who killed a lion and a bear and Goliath the giant.

13.5.5.en: The decisive moment drew near, and Judith looked at the head of the bed and found the dagger of Holofernes hanging, tied to the post of the bed, on the side of Holofernes' head. She untied it and held it in her right hand, and stretched out her left hand courageously and took hold of the hair of Holofernes and lifted it from the pillow, while he was sunk in his sleep, completely unconscious. She lifted her heart in a prayer seeking God's help, that He might support her with His power in this terrible moment, and with all her strength she struck his neck from behind twice, and separated his head from his body, and his blood flowed abundantly.

13.5.6.en: After that she threw the dagger from her, and with her right hand pulled down the canopy of Holofernes' bed and wrapped his head in it, and set it to one side. Then she rolled his body off the bed and let it down to the ground. Thus the mighty man fell at the feet of Judith, as Satan falls under the feet of the striving children of God. Judith here is a type of Christ, who triumphed over Satan by the Cross.

13.5.7.en: The killing here is not a crime, because it is self-defense. She is rescuing herself and her people from Holofernes the tyrant, who came to besiege the city and kill those in it, and killing is permitted in wars, because it is self-defense. Holofernes dies by his own dagger. Instead of killing the children of God with this dagger, he is killed by it. Thus God delivers His children, while the evil of the wicked comes upon their own heads.

13.5.8.en: Here Judith shines in the Holy Bible above many of the heroes who killed enemies. Ehud, who killed Eglon (Judg 3:20-22), was a man of war, but Judith, the gentle woman, received extraordinary strength from God that made her braver than men of war. And Jael, who killed Sisera (Judg 4:

13.5.9.en: 17-22) did so with Sisera, who was fleeing and hiding in her tent in fear, but Judith was in the midst of the camp of the enemies, with no weapon but the power of God.

13.5.10.en: Do not make peace with sin, but cut it off with all force, and confirm your cutting it off more than once. Separate the head of the serpent from its body, and cut off its head, to be rid of its poisons, that is, to be rid of the main source of sin. Be strong and take courage, for by the power of your God you can overcome the devil, and he will be humbled at your feet.

13.5.11.en: (2) Judith's arrival at her city and her proclaiming of the good news (vv. 11-21)

13.5.12.en: 11- And after a little while she went out and handed her maidservant the head of Holofernes and commanded her to put it in her bag.

13.5.13.en: 12- And the two of them went out according to their custom, as though going out to pray, and passed through the camp and went around the valley until they came to the gate of the city. 13- And Judith cried out from afar to the keepers of the wall, Open the gates, for God is with us, and has shown power in Israel. 14- And when the men heard her voice, they called the elders of the city. 15- And they all hastened to her, from the least of them to the greatest, for they had not hoped that she would return. 16- Then they lit lamps and gathered around her, all of them, and she went up to the highest place and commanded silence, and when they were all silent,

13.5.14.en: 17- Judith said, Praise the Lord our God, who has not forsaken those who trust in Him. 18- And by me His handmaid He has fulfilled His mercy which He promised to the house of Israel, and has slain by my hand the enemy of His people this night. 19- Then she took the head of Holofernes out of the bag and showed it, saying, Behold the head of Holofernes, the chief of the army of the Assyrians, and this is the canopy of his bed in which he lay in his drunkenness, where the Lord our God smote him by the hand of a woman. 20- As the Lord liveth, He hath kept me by His angel in my going from here and in my staying there and in my coming back here, and the Lord did not permit His handmaid to be defiled, but brought me back to you without the stain of sin, rejoicing in His victory and my deliverance and yours. 21- Give thanks to Him, all of you, for He is good, for His mercy endureth for ever.

13.6.0.en: A little while: a few moments.

13.6.1.en: Her bag: a cloth sack in which she carried food.

13.6.2.en: Judith looked at the body lying on the ground and the head wrapped in the canopy of the bed, and she stood for a short time thanking God, contemplating with wonder and pride the great work of God.

13.6.3.en: Then she hurried to complete her task. She took up the head wrapped in the canopy of the bed, and lifted the curtain of the tent that separates the bedchamber from the place of reception, and found her maidservant alone. She asked her to open her bag in which she had brought the food, and she put the head of Holofernes in it.

13.6.4.en: Here appears the role of Judith's maidservant, who accompanied her in this difficult mission, and who had probably been close to her throughout the years of her widowhood, sharing her prayers, her fasts and her worship. Judith had chosen her because she trusted her, because she worshipped God faithfully and because she kept secrets. Perhaps Judith had disclosed to her some of the steps of this mission, and the maidservant shared with Judith the three days of prayers and fasts while she was with Holofernes; perhaps the two of them encouraged one another, remembering the power of God and His care for His people. Then the decisive moment came, and the maidservant stood watching and observing those who passed around the tent from a distance, full of faith in the power of God who was keeping them. Now, with a strong heart, she faced the work of God and the success of her mistress in cutting off the head of Holofernes. She was not shaken, but opened her bag to put the head of this wicked man in it. She went out with Judith, reached Bethulia, and shared with her in bringing the good news of God's victory to her people, and she continued to share her mistress's worship and life of solitude all her days. Because of the greatness of her faith, Judith set her free, yet she continued to enjoy Judith's companionship all her days. She is an example of the spiritual servant who cares for spiritual discipleship and obedience, so that her faith grows and she rises to high spiritual levels.

13.7.0.en: Then the two of them went out of the tent and found no one, for everyone was either busy eating or weighed down with drink inside their tents. They passed between the tents until they reached the end of the camp, and went down into the valley leading to Bethulia. Perhaps some of the guards at the edge of the camp saw them, but no one suspected them, since they were used to seeing them go out to bathe at the springs of water near Bethulia during the previous three days, in addition to Bagoas' order to allow them to bathe this night also. Then they continued on their way and disappeared from the sight of the soldiers, until they reached the gates of the city.

13.8.0.en: Then Judith called to the keepers of the gate and to those on the wall of the city, saying to them:

13.8.1.en: Open the gates, for our God has done a great work.

13.8.2.en: God, who was glorified by the hand of this woman, weak in body and strong in faith, is of course able to complete His work, so that no one will stop them or suspect them.

13.8.3.en: If you have conquered the devil in your struggle and have left some sin, do not let the devil make you doubt, suggesting the possibility of falling again; rather be strong and take courage, and complete your striving until you reach the gates of the great city in which the children of God dwell, Bethulia, which points to the heavenly Jerusalem. Then you will be able to call to the keepers, as the angels called - those who ascended with the Spirit of the victorious Christ, who bound the devil on the Cross - to the keepers of Paradise, which had been closed for ages before man, to open so that the Son of Man, Christ our God, might enter as the representative of all humanity, opening and preparing the way after Him for all who believe in Him; and they said, "Lift up your heads, O ye gates; and be ye lift up, ye everlasting doors; and the King of glory shall come in" (Ps 24:7). The head of Holofernes, who was proud and exalted himself over all the nations, indeed over God and His people Israel, and destroyed many with might and tyranny, and cast peoples far from their cities, is carried by a weak maidservant in her bag, that is, her sack.

13.8.4.en: Do not be proud of your strength and of what you have achieved, and do not boast over others, lest God's longsuffering toward you come to an end and you be humbled and carried where you do not wish, by the hand of the one who seems weakest to you.

13.9.1.en: The gatekeepers and the guards of the walls were astonished when they heard the voice of Judith, for they had given up hope of her return. They had thought that she had undertaken a reckless adventure and that she would surely perish or become one of the enemy's slave girls. When they were certain that it was Judith and her maidservant, they hurried to open the gates and received her with great joy.

13.9.2.en: They hurried to call the elders of the city to meet her. The elders woke up and the news spread throughout the whole city, and all the people ran hastily to the city square, asking eagerly about what she had done with the Assyrians, how she had returned, and what the Assyrians had done to her. They brought torches to light the place, and Judith went up to a high place with her maid beside her, and signaled to everyone to be silent. They fell silent, longing to know what had happened at her hands: had she been able to reach an understanding with the enemies, or had she failed and escaped from their hands in disappointment, especially as thirst had overcome them, for this was the fourth day and only one day remained of the delay they had set for Uzziah, the ruler of the city, to surrender the city before they died of thirst. This is the Church gathered around the servants of God to hear His word, and the servant, whom Judith signifies, stands to give the joyful good news to all the people. Judith also signifies Christ, who triumphed over the devil and rose from the dead, proclaiming salvation to everyone who believes in Him; for Judith triumphed over Holofernes, and she is now proclaiming to her city their deliverance from the enemies.

13.9.3.en: Do you bring joyful good news to all around you? If you are striving on the way with God, you will experience His work, and then you will be able to encourage all around you by the grace and power of God. The opposite is also true: if you are harsh in your speech and do not encourage those around you, you have not yet known the way of spiritual striving.

13.10.0.en: Judith called all the people to thank God and praise Him, because He did not forsake His children who trust in Him, however great their weakness and the strength of their enemies, but He supports and rescues all who believe in Him.

13.11.0.en: Then she continued speaking with great humility, declaring that she was not a courageous heroine but a weak handmaid, by whose hand God, out of His love and humility, accomplished His mercy toward His people in Bethulia, and indeed in all Judea. This is the mercy that He promised them by the mouth of His prophets and His saints.

13.11.1.en: Here appears the humility of Judith, who did not ascribe any glory to herself in this great victory, but ascribed faith and trust in God to all the people, although the faith of the people was weak and they wanted to surrender the city; it was she who made them stop by the strength of her faith, and because of this certainty God gave them the victory.

13.11.2.en: The greatest power that overthrows Satan is humility, so that God is glorified and the devil is defeated. Hold fast to humility during your striving, and after your victory, when you thank God and encourage the hearts of those around you.

13.12.0.en: Then she announced the great news that God had destroyed Holofernes by her hand. She looked at her maidservant and took out of her bag the head of Holofernes, wrapped in the canopy of his bed, and held it by the hair and raised it before them, saying: This is the head of Holofernes, the chief of the army of the Assyrians. She told them how he perished, when he indulged in drink until he was drunk and lost consciousness and lay down on his bed, and she cut off his head and took the canopy of his bed and wrapped it in it. Thus God destroyed this great commander by the hand of a weak woman, and she affirmed her humility a second time and ascribed the glory to God; for a woman overcoming a man and killing him is regarded as something strange because of the physical strength of man, how much more so when a weak woman kills the commander of a great army while he is in his camp and among his soldiers.

13.12.1.en: Give those around you the proof of the truth of your good news. The proof is the devil humbled under your feet: his head is cut off, that is, he has no power, through your holding fast to virtue, purity, truthfulness and faithfulness. Let the devil have no authority over you, and let sin be humbled under your feet. That is, be an example and a joyful good news to every person, always directing thanks and glory to God for the good conduct He has granted you, which rises above the conduct of the world around you.

13.13.1.en: Then Judith continued her good news to all the people, that is, to the Church, and to all of us. She said that, by human reasoning, for this victory to be accomplished by the hand of a beautiful woman, she would have to pass through thousands of strong, wicked men who would capture her, and stay with them for three days, and even enter the bedchamber of a mighty, powerful man immersed in drinking wine; she would surely be harmed and exposed to terrifying dangers, and would of necessity be violated and lose her purity. But the mighty God sent His angel from the time she left her city, Bethulia, and he walked with her all along her way, and even stayed with her and kept her in all her meetings with the wicked, even in the bedchamber of this wicked man, so that no one touched her with harm, nor was her purity stained. Thus Judith achieved in her difficult mission three victories:

13.13.2.en: 1- Her keeping her purity among lustful wicked men, by the keeping of God's angel.

13.13.3.en: 2- The killing of the chief of the enemy's armies, and consequently the spreading of terror afterward in the hearts of his army, so that they fled.

13.13.4.en: 3- The rescue of her people from destruction, and even their seizing very many spoils.

13.14.0.en: She asked them to rejoice with her in the salvation of the Lord and to glorify Him, because He magnified His work toward them and kept her and kept them; He is truly good, and His mercy endures for ever. This wonderful hymn is repeated in Psalm 135, which the Church recites in her daily praise and which is called the Second Hoos, or the Second Praise.

13.14.1.en: God is able not only to solve your problems in the midst of affliction in peace, but to bring you out of it purer, cleaner and more loving toward God, so that you are purified from your sins and become more closely bound to God. Then do not forget to lift up praise and thanksgiving to God; rather, make your prayer a daily praise before Him for His former works with you.

13.14.2.en: Do not be afraid to undertake difficult services if the necessity is laid upon you, and trust that God's angel will keep you and make you succeed, and will save many souls by your hands, and will save you first, so that you rejoice and praise God.

13.14.3.en: (3) Glorifying of Judith by the people and Achior (vv. 22-31)

13.14.4.en: 22- And they all worshipped the Lord and said to her, The Lord has blessed you by His power, for by you He has brought our enemies to nothing.

13.14.5.en: 23- And Uzziah, the ruler of the people of Israel, said to her, Blessed art thou, daughter, of the Lord God Most High above all the women upon the earth. 24- Blessed be the Lord God, who created the heavens and the earth, who directed thy hand to the cutting off of the head of the chief of our enemies.

13.14.6.en: 25- For this day He has so magnified thy name that thy praise shall not depart from the mouths of men who remember the power of the Lord for ever, for whose sake thou hast not spared thy life, because of the affliction and distress of thy race, but hast turned away destruction before our God.

13.14.7.en: 26- And all the people said, So be it, so be it. 27- Then they called Achior, and he came, and Judith said to him, The God of Israel, to whom thou hast borne witness that He avenges Himself of His enemies, has cut off this night by my hand the head of all the unbelievers. 28- And that thou mayest know that it is so, behold the head of Holofernes, who despised the God of Israel in the arrogance of his pride, and threatened thee with death, saying, When the people of Israel are taken, I will command that they pierce thy sides with the sword. 29- When Achior saw the head of Holofernes, he was seized with terror and fell on his face on the ground, and his soul was troubled. 30- And after his spirit returned to him and he was revived, he fell down before her, worshipping her, and said, 31- Blessed art thou by thy God in all the tents of Jacob, and in every nation which shall hear of thy name, the God of Israel shall be magnified because of thee.

13.15.0.en: When the people heard this joyful news, they rejoiced and were glad, just as the disciples rejoiced when they saw the Lord Christ in the upper room after His resurrection from the dead, victorious. So Judith signified Christ risen from the dead.

13.15.1.en: Then they expressed their thanks and submission to God by all bowing down before Him, as the twenty-four elders bow down before God in the heavenly Jerusalem.

13.15.2.en: And after they had blessed God, they glorified Judith also, because God blessed her, worked in her by His power and destroyed their enemies by her.

13.15.3.en: God is glorified in His saints, and He is ready to bless you and work through you, if you humble yourself, submit to Him and hold fast to your faith in Him.

13.16.0.en: In the same way Uzziah, the ruler of the city, spoke on behalf of the people, blessing Judith from the Lord and exalting her above all the women of the earth, because there is no faith like this in all the world.

13.16.1.en: If you have faith, God will be glorified through you, and in proportion to your faith the work of the Lord is magnified in you and through you.

13.17.0.en: Directed thy hand: held thy hand and aimed it to strike Holofernes, or used thy hand to kill him.

13.17.1.en: Then Uzziah glorified God, who strengthened this weak woman to kill the greatest and fiercest of the world's brave men at that time - Holofernes - the enemy of the people of God, who wanted to destroy them. The truth is that what defeated Holofernes was his evil lusts, and what sustained Judith was her chastity and her trust in God, so that He worked through her with power and gave her victory for the sake of her purity, as St. Jerome pointed out. The power of God is above every power, and He is able to work the greatest works through a weak human being, as He was born of the humble Virgin, being God incarnate; as all Jerusalem submitted to John the Baptist, who had stripped himself of everything in the wilderness; and as God overcame tens of thousands of enemies by Gideon and the three hundred men.

13.18.0.en: Uzziah declared that on this day the name of Judith is joined to the names of the prophets and the holy men of God, so that all the faithful may remember them with glory and honor throughout the generations, because she is a living example of sacrifice, courage and strength of faith, for she threw herself into the camp of the enemies for the sake of God and the rescue of her people; so God was glorified through her and turned evil and destruction away from His people.

13.19.0.en: When the people heard the words of Uzziah, they declared their agreement with all that he said, saying, Amen, Amen.

13.19.1.en: How beautiful it is to bless God and glorify Him, and how great to praise Him in His saints and recall His works in them throughout the past generations. Strengthen yourself with praise, and you will grow stronger in your spiritual striving. Take part in the praise of the Church, to join the procession of the heroes who strive and triumph over sin.

13.20.0.en: Achior the Ammonite was not present among them at the time when they rejoiced at the good news of Judith. So they sent for him and brought him, and he came quickly, for he had learned of Judith's return, and his heart was filled with fear and joy when he saw the crowd of people in the square and Judith standing on a high platform in their midst. As soon as he reached Judith, she said to him that the God of Israel, to whose power thou didst bear witness before Holofernes, and whose power no man can resist, had been glorified this day by my hand, for He cut off the head of all the wicked who stood against the people of God, since Holofernes was the head and chief of all the armies of the Assyrians.

13.21.0.en: And Holofernes, who insulted God, the God of Israel, and made light of His power, affirming his victory over God and His people and his seizing of Bethulia and indeed all Judea, and who would then have seized thee and killed thee in the most terrible manner by piercing thy sides with his sword - this Holofernes, God has cut off his head by my hand.

13.22.0.en: His soul was troubled: his soul was greatly disturbed.

13.22.1.en: She showed him the head of Holofernes. Achior, who knew him well, had never imagined seeing this head, so lofty and haughty toward everyone, in such humiliation and disgrace, held up by its hair in the hand of a woman. So he was struck with great fear before the power of God at the hands of Judith, and fell on his face and lost consciousness from the excess of his fear.

13.22.2.en: If you are a powerful ruler with authority, or a father who shepherds his household, do not rush ahead in pride, whatever your position, threatening those beneath you with your authority and lording it over them; rather fear God with humility, lest He humble you. And be sure, believer and servant, that God will show forth your right, however much the wicked oppose you, make light of you and threaten you, warning you of evil. Stand firm on the promises and the word of God, and He will keep you.

13.23.0.en: His spirit returned to him: his spirit came back to him, that is, he recovered from his fainting.

13.23.1.en: The tents of Jacob: an expression common at that time, meaning all the people of Israel, who lived in tents for forty years in the wilderness of Sinai, and like Jacob their father, who lived in a tent all his life.

13.23.2.en: Achior recovered from his fainting, turned toward Judith and bowed down before her, declaring his submission to God, bearing witness to her holiness and the great strength of her faith, and declaring that from this day she would be honored and her standing great among all the people of God, and indeed among the peoples of the world who would hear her story and glorify God because of her life and her faith.

13.23.3.en: Does your life glorify God, bear witness to Him and draw many souls to Him, even those far from the faith? God is ready to give you spiritual dignity in the eyes of all, so that they bow before you and honor you and glorify God in you.

13.23.4.en: The terror of the Assyrians at the death of their commander
